📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei has criticized the United States’ role as a host of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, saying the tournament should not become a pretext for discrimination or mistreatment of athletes and representatives of participating nations.

Baghaei, writing in Persian on X on Wednesday, referred to reports of inappropriate treatment of players and coaching staff from some national football teams at US entry points.
​
Football is a platform for fair competition and bringing nations closer together, not an excuse to reopen old grudges and settle political scores, he said. “The World Cup is meant to be a global celebration of football, not an opportunity to humiliate and discriminate against other nations.”
​
The spokesman said reports of improper treatment of players, referees and football guests arriving in the United States stood in contrast to the warm and respectful reception provided by Mexico to visiting teams.
​
Baghaei argued that successful hosting should be measured not by grand stadiums or political publicity, but by the way visitors are treated.
​
“Good hosting is not defined by magnificent venues or political showmanship,” he said. “It is measured by humane behavior and the ability to make guests feel welcome.”
​
He added that a host nation’s reputation is shaped not only by its sporting infrastructure but also by the quality of its treatment of those who travel there for football.
